key_insight: The paper introduces AxiGSIS, an axisymmetric synthetic iterative solver that tightly couples kinetic and macroscopic updates to speed convergence in rarefied gas and charged-particle flows.
engineering_relevance: It offers a faster way to simulate axisymmetric microscale flows under electrostatic forcing, reducing iteration cost while preserving kinetic accuracy.
method: Finite-volume discrete velocity method on a 2D axisymmetric meridian plane with 3D molecular velocity space
Kinetic solver computes stress and heat flux, then passes them as correction terms to a synthetic macroscopic system
Bidirectional feedback updates primitive variables rapidly and feeds the corrected fields back to the kinetic solver
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark validation on four flows, showing agreement with reference kinetic solutions and fewer spatial cells and iterations, especially at low and moderate Knudsen numbers.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on accurate kinetic-to-macroscopic source coupling and careful implementation for strongly non-equilibrium cases.
paper_title: A general synthetic iterative solver for axisymmetric rarefied gas and electrostatic charged-particle flows
